It does not want automatic upgrades when Microsoft changes the default version, but if it misses a retirement date, the deployment must keep working rather than stop. Which `versionUpgradeOption` value should the deployment use?

choices.text: `OnceCurrentVersionExpired`, which keeps the pinned version until its retirement date and then upgrades the deployment to the current default version.
`OnceNewDefaultVersionAvailable`, which upgrades the deployment to the new default version within two weeks of the default version changing.
`NoAutoUpgrade`, which never upgrades the deployment and moves it to the next available model family after its version reaches retirement.
`NoAutoUpgrade`, which keeps the pinned version until its retirement date and then upgrades the deployment to the latest preview version available.

stem: A bank runs a Global Provisioned deployment named `claims-ptu`. It wants to move the deployment to a newer version of the same model while keeping the deployment name, its PTU size and the application's configuration unchanged, and it cannot take an outage. What should the team do?

choices.text: Create a Global Standard deployment with the new version, then change the existing PTU reservation so that it points at that Global Standard deployment.
Perform an in-place migration by updating the model version of `claims-ptu`; Foundry moves traffic over during the migration while the deployment keeps serving requests.
Delete `claims-ptu` and create a new provisioned deployment with the same name and the new version, so the application keeps its configuration after recreation.
Set `versionUpgradeOption` to `OnceNewDefaultVersionAvailable` on `claims-ptu`, so the provisioned deployment switches versions automatically during the next maintenance window.

stem: A platform engineer's Bicep template adds a `GlobalStandard` deployment of a chat model to a new Foundry resource in East US. The deployment fails with an insufficient quota error. The subscription already has two `GlobalStandard` deployments of the same model in East US, in other Foundry resources, plus a deployment of a different model. Which action lets the new deployment get its capacity?

choices.text: Move the new deployment into a different Foundry resource in East US, because each Foundry resource receives its own separate quota for every model it deploys.
Set a `rateLimits` value in the deployment properties of the template, because an explicit rate limit lets the deployment run outside the subscription's model quota.
Lower `sku.capacity` on the deployment of the different model in East US, because capacity released by any model goes back to one shared quota pool for the region.
Lower `sku.capacity` on one of the existing `GlobalStandard` deployments of the same model in East US, or request a quota increase for that model, region and deployment type.

stem: A Foundry resource hosts five team projects. Every project must use the company's shared Azure AI Search index of product documentation, while the finance team's connection to a Storage account of payroll files must be usable only from the finance project. Where should the platform team create the two connections?

choices.text: Create the Azure AI Search connection in each of the five projects and the Storage connection on the Foundry resource, because resource-level connections are visible only to administrators.
Create both connections on the finance project, because connections created in one project are inherited by the other projects that share the same Foundry resource.
Create the Azure AI Search connection on the Foundry resource and the Storage connection on the finance project, because parent-level connections are available to all projects.
Create both connections on the Foundry resource, because connections can be created only at the resource level and each project then selects which connections it shows.

stem: A team manages its Foundry resource, project, model deployments and connections with the Terraform AzureRM provider. It now needs to configure the capability host that points agents at the team's own Storage, Azure AI Search and Cosmos DB resources for the standard agent setup. How should it extend the configuration?

choices.text: Upgrade the AzureRM provider and set the capability host as a nested block on the Foundry account resource, because current AzureRM versions manage it directly.
Create the capability host by running `terraform import` on the existing project, because importing the project brings its agent storage settings into state.
Add an `azapi_resource` for the capability host, because the AzAPI provider exposes all Foundry control plane settings while AzureRM covers only core management.
Replace Terraform with an ARM template export of the resource, because capability hosts can be configured only in templates exported from the Azure portal.

stem: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys a Bicep template that creates a Foundry resource, a project and agent capability settings pointing at an existing Azure Storage account, Azure AI Search service and Azure Cosmos DB account. Which TWO actions are required for the deployment to authenticate securely and succeed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Grant the deployment principal Storage Blob Data Contributor on the Storage account and Cosmos DB Operator on the Cosmos DB account before running the deployment.
Store the Foundry resource API key as a repository secret, because Bicep uses the key to create projects and capability settings on the Foundry resource.
Assign the deployment principal only Foundry User at the project scope, because that role includes the rights to create resources and their role assignments.
Grant the deployment principal Search Index Data Contributor on the search service, because capability settings provisioning fails without a caller data role on search.
Sign in with the Azure Login action using OpenID Connect and a federated credential on the deployment identity, so no client secret is stored in the repository.

stem: A project was created with the basic agent setup, so agent conversations are stored in Microsoft-managed storage. Compliance now requires that conversations, files and vector stores live in the company's own Cosmos DB, Storage and Azure AI Search accounts. An engineer's attempt to update the project's capability settings fails. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Change the model deployment type to Data Zone Standard, so that agent conversations are stored at rest inside the company's chosen data zone.
Create a new project whose capability settings reference the company's resources and recreate the agents, since a project's settings can't be updated.
Add a Cosmos DB connection at the Foundry resource level, so the agents in the existing project move their stored conversations to it automatically.
Edit the capability-settings-managed connection on the project so that it points to the company's Cosmos DB account instead of the managed store.

stem: A team's legacy prompt agent used the project's shared agent identity for its Azure AI Search tool. The team recreates it in the current agent object model, where each new agent gets its own Microsoft Entra agent identity, with the same definition. The new agent's search calls now fail with authorization errors. What is the fix?

choices.text: Regenerate the Azure AI Search admin key and add it to the project connection, because new agents can authenticate tools only with keys.
Assign the Foundry User role to every developer on the project, because tool calls run with the identity of whoever created the agent version.
Restore the original legacy agent's definition on the new agent, because the search tool reads its credentials from the agent's tool configuration.
Assign the required Azure AI Search roles to the new agent's own identity, because role assignments made to the shared project identity don't transfer to it.

stem: A legal team uses a non-reasoning chat model deployment in Microsoft Foundry to draft clause summaries for contracts. Reviewers complain that the same clause gets differently worded summaries on every run, sometimes with invented qualifiers. The developer currently sends temperature 1.2 and top_p 0.9. Following Microsoft's prompt engineering guidance, what should the developer change?

choices.text: Raise top_p to 1.0 while keeping temperature at 1.2, so the model considers every possible token and settles on the most likely wording
Lower the temperature to a small value such as 0.2 and leave top_p at its default, changing only one of the two sampling parameters at a time
Keep the sampling values and raise the maximum output tokens instead, because short output limits are what make the summaries vary between runs
Lower both temperature and top_p to 0 at the same time, because the two parameters must always be moved together to have any effect on output

stem: A procurement team wants a Foundry solution that assesses each new supplier application from four angles: financial health, security posture, legal terms and sustainability. Each check uses its own specialist agent and tools, no check needs another check's output, and the combined verdict is needed within minutes. Which orchestration pattern fits best?

choices.text: Handoff orchestration in which the financial agent starts and transfers full control to whichever specialist it decides should handle the application next
Magentic orchestration in which a manager agent builds and keeps adapting a task ledger, because the four checks have no predetermined solution path
Concurrent orchestration that sends the same application to all four agents in parallel and then aggregates their independent results into one verdict
Sequential orchestration that passes the application through the four agents in a fixed order, so each agent refines the previous agent's finished assessment

stem: A developer sends a JSON Schema with strict set to true for structured outputs. The object has properties name, email and phone; only name and email are listed in "required" because phone is optional, and the object doesn't set additionalProperties. The request is rejected as an invalid schema. Which TWO changes make the schema valid for structured outputs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Replace the object with an anyOf at the root level, because a root anyOf lets the model choose freely between a version with and without phone
Add "minLength": 7 and a "pattern" regular expression to phone, because strict mode needs every string property to have explicit limits
Remove strict from the request and keep the schema as it is, because strict mode is only supported for function calling and not response formats
Set "additionalProperties": false on the object, because structured outputs need every object to forbid keys that the schema doesn't define
List phone in "required" as well and give it the type ["string", "null"], so the model can return null when no phone number exists

stem: A team moves a ticket-triage app from the Chat Completions API to the Responses API in Microsoft Foundry. In the old code, the JSON Schema for structured outputs was passed in response_format. Where does the schema go in a Responses API request?

choices.text: Under text.format, with type, name, schema and strict set as sibling properties of format in the Responses API request body
In the deployment's guardrail settings in the Foundry portal, which apply the schema to every request made to that model deployment
In a tools entry of type function with strict set to true, because the Responses API accepts schemas only as function definitions
In the instructions string as a pasted JSON Schema, because the Responses API reads output formats only from the instructions text of the request

stem: A developer switches a Chat Completions app from a non-reasoning model deployment to a reasoning model deployment. The existing request code sends temperature 0.3, top_p 0.9 and max_tokens 800, and the new deployment rejects the requests. Which TWO changes should the developer make? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Replace max_tokens with max_completion_tokens and size it to cover both the visible answer and the model's reasoning tokens
Rename the system message role to "assistant", because reasoning models accept instructions only through assistant-role messages
Set the frequency_penalty and presence_penalty parameters to 0, because reasoning models require explicit penalty values on every call
Add a "Think step by step" sentence to the user message, because reasoning models need that phrase before they produce any reasoning
Remove the temperature and top_p parameters from the request, because reasoning models don't support these sampling parameters

stem: A company runs two features on the same reasoning model deployment: a voice assistant that classifies each caller utterance into one of ten intents and must answer within a fraction of a second, and an overnight job that debugs failing build logs where accuracy matters far more than time. How should the developer set reasoning_effort?

choices.text: Leave reasoning_effort unset for both features, because every reasoning model defaults to the highest effort level the model supports
Use high for the voice classification so every intent is checked carefully, and none for the build-log job because it runs overnight anyway
Use none or low for the voice classification, and high for the overnight build-log debugging where quality outweighs latency
Use the same medium value for both features, because reasoning_effort only changes the cost of a request and has no effect on its latency

stem: A Responses API call to a reasoning model returns status "incomplete" with incomplete_details.reason "max_output_tokens", and output_text is empty. The usage shows almost all output tokens as reasoning tokens. The request sets max_output_tokens to 600. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Add temperature 0 to the request, because a deterministic model spends fewer reasoning tokens and finishes within the same output limit
Raise max_output_tokens to leave room for reasoning plus the answer, and check status on every response so incomplete results are handled
Move the request to a guardrail with lower severity thresholds, because filtered reasoning tokens are dropped and leave the answer empty
Switch the deployment to a different region, because an incomplete status means the model ran out of regional capacity during the request

stem: A prompt begins with the instruction "Reply in Korean and list at most five action items", followed by a 6,000-word English meeting transcript. The model often answers in English with ten or more items. Which change does Microsoft's prompt engineering guidance suggest trying first?

choices.text: Move the transcript into the system message and leave the user message empty, so the model treats the transcript itself as its standing rules
Shorten the instruction to a single word, "Korean", because shorter instructions are weighted more heavily than longer ones by the model
Increase the temperature so the model is more willing to switch languages, and add a stop sequence after the fifth action item in the reply
Repeat the instruction after the transcript and end with a cue such as "Action items (Korean, max 5):" to prime the expected output

stem: A pharmacy support app passes a few policy excerpts to a model and asks it to answer staff questions. Audits find answers that state plausible but invented rules. The system message already says "Do not make things up." Which prompt change does Microsoft's guidance recommend to reduce fabricated statements?

choices.text: Repeat "Do not make things up" three times in the system message, because repeated prohibitions are the documented fix for fabricated rules
Ask the model to add a numbered list of every source excerpt it relied on at the very end of the reply, after the full answer is written out
Ask the model to put an inline citation to the supporting excerpt next to each statement, and to reply "not found" when the excerpts don't answer
Remove the policy excerpts from the prompt so the model relies only on its training data, which is more consistent than short excerpts

stem: A newsroom tool asks a non-reasoning model, in one prompt, to fact-check a 2,000-word article and propose search queries. Results are vague and skip many claims. Using techniques from Microsoft's prompt engineering guidance, how should the developer restructure the work?

choices.text: Ask the model to pick the three most interesting claims only, because models handle fact-checking best when they choose their own scope
Raise the maximum output tokens and keep the single prompt, because vague results mean the model ran out of room before listing every claim
Translate the article into a shorter bulleted summary first and fact-check the summary, which keeps all claims while using fewer tokens
Break the task down: first have the model list each factual claim in a set format, then generate a search query for each listed claim

stem: Every request in a support app starts with the same 3,000-token system message and product policy, followed by the customer's question. The app currently puts a timestamp and the customer's name at the very top of the system message. The team wants lower latency and input cost on Azure OpenAI without changing answers. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Put the unchanging system message and policy first and move the timestamp and customer name after them, so requests share an identical prefix
Move the policy into a separate request sent before each question, so the model keeps the policy in memory for the next request it receives
Shuffle the order of the policy sections on every request, so the cache treats each request as new and recalculates fresh token computations
Lower max_completion_tokens to 100 on every request, because prompt caching only applies when the requested output length is short

stem: A marketing app generates product descriptions that must pass brand rules (tone, banned claims, length). The team adds a second model call that reviews each draft and sends specific feedback back to the generator, which revises it. In testing, some drafts bounce back and forth for dozens of rounds. Which design matches the maker-checker pattern that Microsoft describes?

choices.text: Remove the review step and raise the generator's temperature instead, so later drafts differ enough from earlier ones to satisfy the rules
The checker scores each draft against the defined brand criteria and the loop ends when it approves or reaches a maximum iteration limit
Have the checker approve every draft after the first round, because a single round of feedback is always enough for the maker to fix it
Let the generator review its own draft in the same call and approve it, because one model judging its own work avoids the extra review calls

stem: Compliance reviewers want to see how a model reached its answers in two Foundry apps: one uses a non-reasoning chat model for tariff classification, the other uses a reasoning model through the Responses API for contract analysis. Which TWO approaches follow Microsoft's guidance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: For both apps, read the reasoning tokens from the usage object, which returns the full reasoning text alongside the count of reasoning tokens
For the non-reasoning model, ask it to work step by step and then give the final result in a fixed format such as "ANSWER is: <code>"
For the non-reasoning model, raise the temperature to its maximum so the reply shows several different reasoning paths for reviewers to compare
For the reasoning model, add a prompt that tells it to print its complete hidden reasoning tokens verbatim before it writes the final answer
For the reasoning model, request a reasoning summary with the reasoning.summary parameter of the Responses API and store it with the answer

stem: A travel firm's Foundry app must classify incoming emails into one of six request types and pass each to the right existing back-office queue. An architect proposes a multiagent design with a planner agent, a classifier agent and a reviewer agent. According to Microsoft's orchestration guidance, what should the team build first?

choices.text: A magentic orchestration in which a manager agent builds a dynamic plan for each email, because the types may change in future years
A concurrent orchestration that sends every email to six agents in parallel, one per request type, and keeps whichever agent replies first
A group chat of all three agents with a chat manager, because classification decisions are most reliable when several agents debate them
A direct model call with a well-crafted prompt (and structured output) that classifies the email, with code routing it to the queue

stem: A loan pre-screening app uses a model to read applicant letters. Regulators require that the approve or decline decision follow published rules (income ratio, credit band) exactly and be reproducible. How should the developer combine the model with those rules?

choices.text: Ask a reasoning model at high reasoning effort to decide, because its hidden reasoning steps are logged as an auditable record of each rule
Fine-tune the model on past approve and decline decisions so the published rules are encoded in its weights and applied automatically
Use structured outputs to extract fields such as income and credit band, validate them, and apply the published rules in deterministic code
Put the published rules in the system message and let the model make the final approve or decline decision, setting temperature to 0 for consistency

stem: An insurer automates claim letters with three Foundry agents: one extracts facts from the claim form, one checks those facts against the policy wording, and one drafts the customer letter from the checked result. Each stage needs the complete output of the stage before it, and the order never changes. Which design follows Microsoft's orchestration guidance?

choices.text: Sequential orchestration in the fixed order extract, check, draft, with each stage's output validated before it is passed on to the next agent in the chain
Group chat orchestration in which a chat manager lets all three agents discuss the claim in one shared thread until they agree on the final customer letter
Handoff orchestration that lets each agent decide at run time which agent should take over next, because the three agents hold different specialist knowledge
Concurrent orchestration that starts all three agents at once on the claim form and merges their outputs, because parallel agents reduce the total run time

stem: Application Insights is connected to a Foundry project and agent traffic is flowing. A developer who has the Foundry User role on the project opens the Traces view and gets an authorization error when the portal queries telemetry. What is the most likely fix?

choices.text: Switch the agents from server-side tracing to client-side tracing, because client-side traces don't need any permissions to read in the portal
Assign the developer the Foundry Owner role on the Foundry resource, because only owners can query traces that the project itself has written
Assign Log Analytics Reader on the connected Application Insights resource, plus Privileged Monitoring Data Reader if its tables are protected
Disconnect and reconnect the Application Insights resource, because each new connection resets the trace data and grants access to every project user

stem: After a prompt change, a non-streaming summarization service on Azure OpenAI shows Time to Last Byte (AzureOpenAITTLTInMS) rising from about 4 to 9 seconds. On-call engineers suspect the deployment is degraded. What should they check first to tell a real regression from expected behavior?

choices.text: The Blocked Volume metric, because content filtering adds most of the per-request time and the new prompt likely triggers more blocks
The Processed Prompt Tokens metric only, because prompt length drives total response time far more than the number of generated tokens
Normalized Time to First Byte, because it gives the absolute response time that users experience regardless of the prompt or reply size
Generated Completion Tokens on the same time range; if it rose with TTLT, the longer replies explain the latency rather than a degradation

stem: Users of a chat assistant complain that they stare at a blank screen for several seconds before anything appears, although full answers finish in an acceptable total time. What should the developer enable and which Azure Monitor metric shows the improvement?

choices.text: Enable streaming (stream: true), and watch Time to Response, which measures the time from prompt submission to the first response chunk
Enable batching of all user requests into one call, and watch Time to Last Byte, because batched calls finish sooner for every user
Enable the n parameter with a value of 3, and watch Tokens per Second, because three parallel answers make the first text appear sooner
Enable prompt caching for the output, and watch Generated Completion Tokens, because cached outputs return without generating any tokens

stem: Auditors require that a Foundry project's agent traces stay queryable for 18 months. Server-side tracing sends traces to a connected workspace-based Application Insights resource, and the Foundry portal's Traces view lists traces from only the last 90 days. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Publish a new agent version every 90 days, because traces belong to an agent version and are deleted as soon as that version is replaced
Extend the analytics retention of the Log Analytics workspace (or its trace tables) behind Application Insights, and query older traces there
Raise the trace retention value in the Foundry project settings to 18 months, because the project keeps its own separate copy of every agent trace
Export the deployment's Azure Monitor platform metrics to a storage account, because those metrics hold the full trace content of each run

stem: A FinOps analyst builds token analytics from the usage object that a reasoning model returns through the Chat Completions API. She needs to know how many output tokens were hidden reasoning and how many input tokens were served from the prompt cache. Which TWO fields should she read? (Select TWO)

choices.text: choices[0].message.reasoning_content, which returns the hidden reasoning text so its tokens can be counted in the analytics job
system_fingerprint, which encodes the number of cached tokens and changes whenever a request is served from the prompt cache
prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, which counts the input tokens that matched the prompt cache instead of being processed again
total_tokens minus prompt_tokens, which gives the reasoning tokens alone because visible output isn't counted in completion tokens
completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens, which counts the reasoning tokens included in the billed output tokens for the request

stem: An agent in a Foundry project occasionally takes 20 seconds to respond instead of 3. Server-side tracing is enabled. The developer wants to find out which step causes the delay in a slow run. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Open the slow run's trace in the Foundry Traces view and compare the durations of its nested spans, such as model calls and execute_tool spans
Read the deployment's Processed Inference Tokens metric for the hour, because a slow run always processed more tokens than a normal run
Turn on a higher reasoning effort for the agent and rerun the request, because more reasoning shows which tool caused the extra latency
Export the agent's conversation history as text and look for long messages, because message length is the only recorded latency signal

stem: A healthcare company enables tracing for its Foundry agents. Security reviewers worry that traces could expose patient details and API secrets that appear in prompts and tool arguments. Which practice follows Microsoft's guidance for tracing?

choices.text: Store API keys as span attributes so failed tool calls can be replayed exactly, and restrict the Traces view to the security team
Send all traces to a public OTLP endpoint for a third-party vendor, because external backends automatically remove personal data from spans
Turn off tracing in production entirely and rely on user complaints, because trace data can never be protected once it leaves the agent
Keep secrets out of prompts and span attributes, redact personal data before it reaches telemetry, and apply log-level access and retention

stem: A high-volume FAQ bot sends simple and occasionally complex prompts. The team wants one Foundry deployment that sends easy prompts to cheaper models and hard prompts to stronger ones, while only ever using three models approved by their compliance team. What should they deploy?

choices.text: A single deployment of the largest approved model with temperature set low, because a stronger model makes routing between models unnecessary
A model router deployment using Custom deploy with the Cost routing mode and a model subset that contains only the three approved models
Three separate model deployments with a load balancer that spreads requests evenly across them, so each model receives a third of the traffic
A model router deployment using Custom deploy with the Quality routing mode and every supported model left in the routing pool

stem: An app calls a model router deployment with temperature 0.2. Some answers look less deterministic than others, and a few requests with very long documents fail with a context exceeded error. What explains both behaviors?

choices.text: When a reasoning model is selected, temperature is ignored, and the router's context limit is that of its smallest underlying model
Model router only uses the first message of each request, so temperature is lost, and long documents are split across several underlying models
Model router caches every answer for a day, so later requests return earlier sampled answers, and long documents exceed the router's cache size
Model router requires the Responses API, so temperature is dropped on Chat Completions, and long documents must be uploaded through file search first

stem: A chat service on a standard Azure OpenAI deployment must cut per-call latency. Profiling shows short chat turns share the deployment with long report-generation calls, and every request sets max_tokens 2500 although chat replies average about 120 tokens. Which TWO changes does Microsoft's latency guidance recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Raise max_tokens to 16000 so the model reserves enough compute in advance and never slows down near the end of a long reply
Set n to 3 on each chat request and display whichever reply finishes first, so users see the fastest of three parallel answers
Set max_tokens on each call as low as the expected reply allows, and add stop sequences so the model doesn't generate extra content
Move the system message to the end of the prompt, because prompt tokens at the start of a request add more latency than generated tokens
Move the report-generation calls to a separate deployment, so short chat calls aren't batched with long completions on one endpoint

stem: A team wants to replace its single direct model deployment with a model router deployment for a document Q&A app. A manager asks how to confirm the switch is worthwhile before moving production traffic, and how to see afterwards which model answered each request. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Trust the router's default Balanced mode without testing, and read the deployment name in each response, which changes to the chosen model's name
Benchmark only latency, because the router always matches the quality of the strongest model, and read the model name from the request headers
Run the router in Quality mode for a week and compare invoices, then read the routing decision from the guardrail annotations in each response
Benchmark the router against the current deployment for quality, cost and latency, then read the model field of each response to see the serving model

stem: A retailer routes customer reviews from its France-only web shop to reviewers by language with Azure Language language detection. Very short reviews such as "Communication" or "Excellent" are often returned as English with a low confidence score. The reviews are almost always French. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Set the language field of each document to "fr", because language detection needs the input language first
Send countryHint set to "fr" with each document, so ambiguous text is resolved with France as the origin
Run key phrase extraction first and send only the returned phrases to language detection for a better score
Transliterate each review to Latin script with Translator first, so the detector can recognize French words

stem: A scheduling assistant reads meeting request emails and must pull out dates, times and money amounts such as "next Friday at 3 pm" or "eighty euros" with character offsets and in a consistent machine-readable form. There is no labeled data, and the team wants a core, non-generative Azure Language feature. Which feature should it call?

choices.text: Key phrase extraction, which returns phrases such as "next Friday" as a plain list without categories or values
Custom named entity recognition, which returns DateTime and Currency entities once labeled emails are used to train it
Prebuilt named entity recognition, which returns DateTime and Currency entities with offsets and resolved metadata
Entity linking, which links every date and amount found in an email to its Wikipedia article to resolve its value

stem: An architect is designing a five-year text analytics platform on Azure Language in Foundry Tools and wants to build only on capabilities that Learn lists as core and recommended for new development. Which TWO capabilities qualify? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Key phrase extraction to return the main concepts in each document as a simple list of phrases
Custom named entity recognition trained on the company's own labeled text to extract new entity types
Sentiment analysis and opinion mining to score how customers feel about specific product features
Conversational language understanding to predict user intents and extract entities from utterances
Personally identifiable information (PII) detection for text, conversations and native documents

stem: A software company wants every piece of customer feedback tagged with one or more topics from its own fixed list of 12 product areas, such as Billing, Onboarding and Mobile app. The tags feed a dashboard, so only values from the list are allowed. This is a new solution. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Call Azure Language language detection first and assign each detected language to one of the 12 product areas
Call Azure Language key phrase extraction and use the returned phrases directly as the topic labels on the dashboard
Call Azure Language entity linking and map each linked Wikipedia article to the nearest of the 12 product areas
Prompt a Foundry chat model with the 12 areas and a strict output schema whose topics array uses an enum of those areas

stem: A help desk stores ticket text in a data lake. Compliance wants only credit card numbers and phone numbers masked; names must stay readable for agents. The team uses Azure Language PII detection with the generally available API. How should the request be configured?

choices.text: Set piiCategories to the credit card and phone number categories so only those entities are detected and masked in redactedText
Leave the categories at their default and remove person names from redactedText afterwards by copying them back from the original text
Send each ticket to Text analytics for health, because it masks financial and contact identifiers while leaving names untouched
Set the language parameter to an unsupported value so the service skips person detection and returns only numeric entities

stem: A law firm must share signed contracts (PDF and DOCX) with an external auditor after removing personal data, and the auditor needs files that keep the original layout plus a machine-readable list of what was removed. Which Azure Language PII feature type fits?

choices.text: Prebuilt NER, which detects people and organizations in text but is designed without any redaction output
Conversation PII, which processes turn-based chat and transcript payloads with conversational context
Text PII, which processes raw strings synchronously and returns the redacted string inside the API response
Document-based PII, which redacts native files asynchronously and returns redacted files with JSON metadata

stem: A hospital group wants to pull medications, dosages, diagnoses and the relations between them out of free-text discharge notes. It has no labeled training data and wants a supported, non-generative service for a new long-term project. Which option should the developer choose?

choices.text: Azure Language entity linking, which disambiguates entities in each note and returns links to Wikipedia pages
Azure Language prebuilt NER, which recognizes general entity types such as Person, Location and DateTime
Azure Language Text analytics for health, which extracts and labels health information from unstructured text
Azure Language custom text classification, which assigns each discharge note to one or more custom categories

stem: An insurer must extract internal entity types (policy rider codes, coverage clause names, adjuster IDs) from claim notes. Auditors require each entity's character offset and a confidence score, and the label set must stay stable across releases. The team has 400 labeled notes. Which approach meets these requirements best?

choices.text: Train an Azure Language custom NER model on the labeled notes and call it for the predicted entities with offsets
Use Azure Language prebuilt NER, because its predefined categories already include rider codes and clause names
Use a chat model prompt that asks for the entities in prose, then search the note text for each returned phrase
Use Azure Language key phrase extraction, then keep the phrases that look like codes, clause names or IDs

stem: A telecom wants support chats labeled with a tone from its own list (polite, frustrated, sarcastic, threatening to cancel) plus a one-line reason for each label. Azure Language sentiment analysis was proposed. What is the best approach for this new project?

choices.text: Use Azure Language opinion mining and treat each aspect it extracts as the tone label for the whole support chat
Prompt a Foundry chat model with tone definitions and a strict schema holding an enum tone field and a reason string
Use Azure Language sentiment analysis and map positive, neutral, negative and mixed results to the four tone labels
Use the guardrails hate and violence categories, because their severity levels already measure customer frustration

stem: A logistics company receives customer names and street addresses in Cyrillic from its Russian web shop. Courier labels must show the same names and streets in Latin letters so that drivers can read them, and the words must not be translated into English. Which Azure Translator operation fits?

choices.text: Synchronous document translation of a DOCX label template, which rewrites Cyrillic text into Latin script in the file
Translate with textType html and each name wrapped in notranslate markup, which writes the names in Latin letters
Transliterate with language ru, fromScript Cyrl and toScript Latn, which changes only the script and keeps the words
Translate with the target language set to en, which returns English words that drivers can read on each courier label

stem: An e-commerce company translates product descriptions with Azure Translator in Foundry Tools. For one premium brand, marketing wants a formal tone in German and French, while millions of standard catalog lines should stay on the cheaper standard path. What should the developer use?

choices.text: A Custom Translator model trained on informal sentences, used for the standard catalog lines and the premium items
The 2026-06-06 text translation API, selecting an LLM deployment for premium items with a formal tone and NMT for the rest
Text translation v3 with a dynamic dictionary that maps every informal German and French word to a formal alternative
Synchronous document translation, because formal tone is available only when whole files are translated at once

stem: A manufacturer must translate 6,000 DOCX and PPTX manuals into Japanese while keeping layout, tables and formatting, and a glossary of part names must be applied. Translation will use asynchronous batch document translation in Azure Translator. Which TWO items must be in place? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A conversion of each manual to plain text first, because batch translation accepts only .txt input files
A Custom Translator model for Japanese, because batch document translation can only run with a custom model
An Azure AI Search index over the manuals, because the service reads source files from a search index
Authorization for the storage URLs, by using shared access signature (SAS) tokens or a managed identity
An Azure Blob Storage account with a source container for the manuals and a target container for the results

stem: A travel site translates hotel descriptions with Translator text translation v3. Hotel brand names such as "Seaview Grand" are being translated literally into other languages. The descriptions are sent as HTML. What is the simplest way to keep the brand names unchanged?

choices.text: Wrap each brand name in an element with class="notranslate", with textType set to html on the translation request
Switch to synchronous document translation, which never translates proper nouns that appear inside HTML files
Train a Custom Translator model with sentences in which the brand names are left untranslated in each target language
Call language detection on each description and skip translation for any sentence that contains a brand name

stem: A legal publisher has 80,000 previously translated English-German sentence pairs in TMX files and wants high-volume neural machine translation that follows its legal terminology and style. Calls go through the Translator text API. Which solution fits?

choices.text: Use Azure Language custom NER on the TMX data to learn legal terms, then pass the entities to standard translation
Send every sentence to a chat model with all 80,000 sentence pairs pasted into the system message as examples
Use document translation with the TMX files uploaded as a glossary, because glossaries replace model training
Train a Custom Translator model on the parallel data, publish it, and pass its category ID on translation requests

stem: A bank's compliance team wants each regulatory notice summarized into fixed sections (Obligation, Deadline, Affected products) that cite the notice's section numbers and never add facts not in the notice. A Foundry chat model is used. Which TWO actions best customize the output for this task? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Use Azure Language abstractive summarization instead, because it accepts custom section names and citation rules
Define a strict output schema with the three sections, each holding text plus an array of cited section numbers
Raise the temperature so that the model paraphrases more freely and avoids copying wording from the notice
Remove the notice text from the prompt and rely on the model's training data to keep summaries short and generic
Put the compliance rules, citation format and one worked example in the system message, and pass the full notice text

stem: A team is choosing between Azure Translator NMT and a prompt-based translation flow on a Foundry chat model for 40 million short UI strings per month in 25 languages. Latency must be predictable and cost must stay low; no tone control is needed. Which recommendation matches Learn's guidance?

choices.text: Use Translator NMT for this high-volume baseline traffic and reserve LLM translation for content that needs tone or context
Use the chat model for all strings, because Translator text translation supports only a handful of language pairs
Use the chat model for all strings, because LLM translation is billed per character at the same rate as Translator NMT
Use Translator NMT only after converting every UI string into a DOCX file for synchronous document translation

stem: A utility company is building a phone-style voice agent. The prototype chains speech to text, a chat model and text to speech by hand, and users complain about lag, the agent hearing its own voice through the speaker, and being cut off during short pauses. Which change addresses all three issues with the least engineering?

choices.text: Keep the chain and add a custom speech model, which removes the agent's own voice from the microphone signal before recognition
Move to batch transcription, which processes the user's audio in parallel across regions to remove lag from each turn
Move to the Voice Live API, which adds echo cancellation, noise suppression and semantic turn detection in one session
Keep the chain and replace text to speech with batch synthesis, which returns audio files more quickly than real-time synthesis

stem: A retailer already has a Foundry Agent Service agent with instructions and tools for order lookups, used in a text chat. It now wants the same agent available by voice, without copying the instructions into the voice client's session code. How should the developer connect the voice channel?

choices.text: Deploy a gpt-realtime model and paste the agent's instructions into each session.update so the voice client behaves the same
Connect Voice Live to the existing agent by its agent name and Foundry project, so the agent's instructions and tools are used
Create a second agent that only transcribes audio and forwards the text by email to the original order lookup agent
Export the agent to a custom speech model, which stores the agent's instructions and tools inside the recognition endpoint

stem: A team trained a custom speech model for zh-CN on an Azure Speech resource in another subscription. In its Voice Live session it sets input_audio_transcription to model azure-speech with a custom_speech entry mapping zh-CN to the model ID, but recognition behaves like the base model. What should the team do?

choices.text: Retrain the custom speech model with text only, because models trained with audio data are not accepted by Voice Live
Move the zh-CN entry into phrase_list, because Voice Live accepts custom speech model IDs only inside the phrase list
Copy the custom speech model to the Microsoft Foundry resource that the application uses to call the Voice Live API
Change the transcription model to whisper-1, because custom speech models are supported only with whisper-1 in Voice Live

stem: A gaming store's voice assistant often mishears about 30 product names such as "TUF Gaming" and "Neo QLED". The list changes weekly and the team has no time to collect audio or train models. Which option improves recognition fastest?

choices.text: Create a professional custom voice so that the assistant pronounces the product names correctly in its spoken replies
Add an SSML lexicon to the text to speech output so that the speech recognizer learns the product names from it
Train a custom speech model with audio of each product name and redeploy a custom endpoint after every weekly change
Pass the product names as a phrase list in the session or recognizer configuration so recognition favors them

stem: A factory's voice-controlled inspection agent runs on a noisy shop floor, and workers use plant-specific jargon. The base speech to text model has a high word error rate (WER). Which TWO steps follow Learn's custom speech process for this problem? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Test the base and custom models on the same test data and compare their WER before deploying the custom model
Raise the chat model's temperature so it guesses the intended jargon more freely from the noisy transcriptions
Add SSML prosody tags to the agent's spoken replies so that the recognizer filters out background machine noise
Train a professional custom voice on the workers' recordings so that recognition adapts to their accents and noise
Train a custom speech model with audio recorded on the shop floor and human-written reference transcripts of it

stem: A legal firm's custom speech model is used only by a nightly job that transcribes the day's recorded depositions with the batch transcription API. Finance asks how to cut speech costs without losing the model. What should the developer recommend?

choices.text: Switch the nightly job to real-time transcription, because only real-time recognition supports custom speech models
Retrain the custom model every night, because custom models expire within a day unless they are trained again
Keep the hosted custom endpoint, because every custom speech model must be deployed before any API can use it
Remove the hosted custom endpoint, because batch transcription can use the custom speech model without a deployed endpoint

stem: A telecom wants voicemail transcripts shown in its app within seconds after each voicemail file is saved. Files are short, one at a time, and the app waits for the result in the same request. Which Azure Speech option fits?

choices.text: Fast transcription, which returns results synchronously and faster than real time for an audio file
Real-time transcription with the Speech SDK, which streams microphone audio and returns interim results
Batch transcription, which schedules jobs on a best-effort basis and stores the results in a container
Text to speech batch synthesis, which converts long voicemail text into audio files asynchronously

stem: A contact center submits 50,000 recorded calls for batch transcription by sending one Transcription_Create request per file at a high rate and polling every job's status every two seconds. Throughput hasn't improved and the API is slow. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Switch every call to fast transcription with a polling loop, because fast transcription is the asynchronous API
Send even more create requests per minute from several threads, because each request adds parallel capacity
Submit many files per create request, spread submissions over time, and check status about every ten minutes
Poll every job more often, because the service starts a waiting job sooner when its status is checked often

stem: A web app lets customers talk to an assistant from the browser by using a deployed gpt-realtime model in Microsoft Foundry. The team wants the lowest possible audio latency for this client-side experience. Which connection method should it use?

choices.text: SIP from the browser, which Learn recommends for web apps because it bypasses the browser audio stack
WebRTC, which Learn recommends for low-latency real-time audio streaming in browser and mobile clients
Batch transcription with a callback, which Learn recommends for browser-based conversational experiences
WebSocket from each browser directly, which Learn recommends as the fastest method for end-user devices

stem: Users of a Realtime API voice assistant say it starts answering whenever they pause briefly to think in the middle of a sentence. The session uses turn_detection of type server_vad with a short silence_duration_ms. Which change best addresses the complaint?

choices.text: Set input_audio_transcription to a transcription model, which stops the assistant from responding during pauses
Remove the tools array from session.update, because tool definitions make the model reply before turns finish
Switch turn_detection to semantic_vad, which ends a turn when the words indicate the user has finished speaking
Change the voice parameter to another built-in voice, because each voice has its own fixed pause threshold

stem: An insurer wants to analyze recorded claim calls in production: who said what, a summary and flags for missing disclosures. The design review requires generally available APIs only. Audio chat completions with gpt-audio were proposed. Which design meets the requirement?

choices.text: Send each call to gpt-audio through chat completions and accept the preview API version for production
Send each call to the Translator text API, which accepts audio files and returns speaker-labeled summaries
Send each call to Azure Language PII detection, which accepts audio files and returns summaries and flags
Transcribe each call with fast transcription and diarization, then analyze the transcript with a chat model

stem: A conference app uses the Speech SDK TranslationRecognizer. It calls add_target_language for German, French and Spanish, sets voice_name to a German voice and handles the synthesizing event, but it gets no usable translated audio for French and Spanish. What is the correct fix?

choices.text: Change speech_recognition_language to each target in turn, because it sets the language of the synthesized audio
Use the translations in each result and synthesize each language with a SpeechSynthesizer whose voice matches that language
Set voice_name to a multilingual French voice, because one voice_name produces audio for every target language at once
Replace TranslationRecognizer with the Translator text API, which returns synthesized audio for up to three languages

stem: A media company has two speech translation needs: live speaker audio at a keynote must be heard in Spanish with low latency, and a library of recorded podcast episodes must become English text. Which TWO pairings are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Podcast library: fast transcription in enhanced mode (Azure LLM Speech) with task translate and targetLanguage en
Live keynote: Translator document translation, which accepts streamed audio and returns translated speech
Live keynote: Azure Language language detection, which converts each detected sentence into Spanish speech
Podcast library: Custom Translator, which trains on audio files to output English text from podcasts directly
Live keynote: Speech SDK speech translation with Spanish as target and a Spanish voice for synthesized output

stem: An education publisher turns 90-minute course texts into narrated audio files with an Azure Speech neural voice. Requests through the real-time synthesis API time out or need to be split by hand. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use fast transcription, which converts long texts to audio synchronously faster than real time on the same request
Use the batch synthesis API, which synthesizes long audio asynchronously so the app polls and downloads the files
Use custom speech with the course texts, which trains the voice to read long texts without hitting request timeouts
Use the Voice Live API, which returns long narration as a single audio file once the WebSocket session is closed

stem: A Voice Live agent recognizes the drink name "Matcha Kiri" correctly, but in its spoken replies the standard Azure voice keeps pronouncing the name wrongly. How should the developer fix the pronunciation?

choices.text: Add "Matcha Kiri" to the phrase_list in input_audio_transcription so that the output voice learns how to say it
Train a custom speech model with recordings of the drink name so the synthesized voice copies the pronunciation
Set custom_lexicon_url in the session's voice configuration to a lexicon that defines how the name is pronounced
Switch turn_detection to azure_semantic_vad so the voice slows down and pronounces product names more carefully

stem: A team built a chunked index in Azure AI Search with an indexer, a Text Split skill and an AzureOpenAIEmbedding skill. Indexing succeeds and the vector field is populated. When the app sends a vector query with "kind": "text" and the user's question, the request fails because the text can't be converted to a vector. What must the team add?

choices.text: A vectorizer in the index's vectorSearch section that calls the same embedding deployment, referenced by the vector field's vector profile
A second AzureOpenAIEmbedding skill in the skillset that runs at query time and writes the embedded question into a temporary field of the index
An indexer field mapping from the chunk text field to the vector field, so the search engine can look up a stored vector for the query string
A semantic configuration that lists the vector field as its content field, so the semantic ranker converts the query text into an embedding first

stem: A search index was built with chunks embedded by text-embedding-3-small through the AzureOpenAIEmbedding skill. To improve quality, a developer changes only the index's Azure OpenAI vectorizer to a text-embedding-3-large deployment. Vector queries now return errors or unrelated chunks. What is the correct fix?

choices.text: Keep the new vectorizer and add the large model to the semantic configuration's keyword fields, so the two embedding spaces are aligned at query time
Keep the new vectorizer and enable semantic ranker on the queries, so the reranking step promotes the relevant chunks to the top of the vector results
Keep the new vectorizer and switch the vector algorithm from HNSW to exhaustive KNN, so every chunk is compared with the query vector and recall improves
Use the same model on both sides: either point the vectorizer back to the small model, or change the skill and field dimensions and re-run indexing

stem: An insurer indexes PDFs from Azure Blob Storage for a RAG app. Many PDFs are scanned forms with no text layer, and their chunks in the index are empty. The team wants to fix this with built-in Azure AI Search features in the existing skillset pipeline. Which two changes are needed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add the OCR skill with its context and image input set to /document/normalized_images/*, then merge its text output into the content before chunking
Raise the Text Split skill's maximumPageLength to 50,000 characters, so scanned pages are kept in one chunk instead of being dropped as too small
Add the Key Phrase Extraction skill before the Text Split skill, so each scanned page gets a list of phrases that the chunking step can split
Set the indexer's parsingMode to markdown, so the blob indexer converts each scanned page into Markdown sections before running the skillset
Set the indexer's imageAction configuration parameter to generateNormalizedImages, so document cracking outputs the page images as normalized images

stem: A parts distributor enriches product sheets in an Azure AI Search skillset. Each sheet must also get a normalized part number from the company's own lookup logic, which already runs as an HTTPS endpoint in Azure Functions. No built-in skill provides this logic. How should the team add it to the pipeline?

choices.text: Add an Azure OpenAI vectorizer that points to the function URL, so the normalized part number is computed whenever a query touches a product sheet
Add a GenAI Prompt skill whose prompt asks a chat model to call the Azure Functions endpoint and copy the normalized part number into its output
Add a Custom Entity Lookup skill and paste the function's normalization rules into the skill's inline entity list, so the lookup runs inside the service
Add a Custom Web API skill whose uri points to the function; it receives a values array of records and must return each recordId with its data

stem: A team is creating a new skillset for long PDF and PPTX reports. Tables often continue across pages and must stay intact in the chunks, and chunks should carry page location metadata. They want a generally available skill that extracts and chunks without a separate Text Split skill. Which skill fits best?

choices.text: The Document Layout skill with outputFormat set to text, which is the recommended choice for new skillsets that need cross-page tables
The OCR skill on normalized page images, whose layoutText output keeps table rows aligned and records the page number for every chunk
The Azure Content Understanding skill, which outputs Markdown chunks with location metadata and keeps cross-page tables together as one unit
The Document Extraction skill with image extraction enabled, followed by the Text Split skill set to sentences mode so tables are kept together

stem: A skillset splits each manual into chunks and embeds them. The team wants one search index where every search document is a chunk, and each chunk repeats the parent manual's title and URL so the RAG app can cite it. Parent-only documents must not appear in the index. How should they configure the skillset?

choices.text: Run two indexers on the same data source, one writing parent documents and one writing chunks, and join them at query time on the parent key
Add indexProjections that target the chunk index, map the parent fields in the selectors, and set projectionMode to skipIndexingParentDocuments
Add a Shaper skill that nests every chunk inside its parent document, and map the shaped object to one complex collection field of the index
Set the indexer's parsingMode to jsonArray, so each chunk produced by the Text Split skill is parsed as a separate document with parent fields

stem: A RAG app answers questions from policy documents chunked by the Text Split skill (textSplitMode pages, maximumPageLength 2000, pageOverlapLength 0). Answers often miss a condition that starts at the end of one chunk and finishes in the next. Which change addresses this most directly?

choices.text: Raise maximumPageLength above the embedding model's input limit, so that each policy document always ends up as one single chunk
Set maximumPagesToTake to 1, so the skill keeps only the first and most complete chunk of each document and discards the fragments
Switch textSplitMode to sentences, so each chunk holds a single sentence and no condition is ever divided between two consecutive chunks
Set pageOverlapLength to about a quarter of the chunk size, so the end of each chunk is repeated at the start of the next one

stem: A RAG app switched from vector-only queries to hybrid queries (text plus a vector query) in Azure AI Search and must keep hybrid retrieval. The app still discards results whose @search.score is below 0.8, a cutoff tuned for cosine similarity. Now every hybrid query passes no chunks to the model, although relevant chunks rank at the top. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Set the vector query's weight to 2.0, so the vector side dominates the fused ranking and @search.score reports the cosine similarity of each chunk again
Raise the vector query's k from 50 to 1,000, so many more vector matches enter the fused list and the top results collect scores above the 0.8 cutoff again
Remove the fixed 0.8 cutoff, because a hybrid @search.score is a Reciprocal Rank Fusion score that is far below 0.8; base any cutoff on semantic ranker scores instead
Change the vector field's similarity metric from cosine to dotProduct in the HNSW configuration, so hybrid @search.score values return to the 0 to 1 range again

stem: A team enables semantic ranker for hybrid queries over a chunk index. The semantic configuration lists title as the title field and a long keywords field first, then the chunk text field, under content. Reranking ignores parts of the chunk text, and captions rarely come from it. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Add the vector field to the semantic configuration's content fields, so reranking uses the embedding of the chunk instead of its text
Put the chunk text field first among the content fields and remove low-value fields, because inputs are trimmed in priority order
Raise the vector query's k to 1,000, so the semantic ranker receives more candidate chunks and finds the passages in the chunk text field
Switch the query to queryType full, so the semantic ranker reads every field of the index instead of the fields listed in the configuration

stem: A product owner reviews a design that adds semantic ranker to an Azure AI Search hybrid query used for grounding a chat model. Which two statements about the semantic ranker are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Its captions and semantic answers are verbatim text taken from the indexed documents, not new text composed by a generative model
It needs the chat model's deployment name in the query request, because it calls that model to compose a direct answer for the user
It replaces the vector search step of a hybrid query, so the index no longer needs a vectorizer once semantic ranking is turned on
It writes a generated summary of each document into the index during indexing, and queries later return that stored summary as the caption
It reads only text, so it can rerank pure vector query results only when the documents also have text fields listed in the semantic configuration

stem: A Foundry agent uses the Azure AI Search tool through a project connection that authenticates with an admin API key. After the security team disables public network access on the search service and adds a private endpoint, the agent, deployed with the standard setup and virtual network injection, fails with "Unable to connect to Azure AI Search Resource". What should the team do?

choices.text: Rotate the admin key and store the new key in Azure Key Vault, then reference the secret from the project connection instead of pasting it
Switch the agent to the basic agent setup, which routes tool calls through the Foundry resource's own managed network to private search services
Re-enable public network access on the search service, because the Azure AI Search tool can't reach a search service through a private endpoint
Switch the connection to Microsoft Entra project managed identity and give that identity Search Index Data Contributor and Search Service Contributor

stem: An HR agent in Foundry Agent Service uses the Azure AI Search tool. Answers are grounded in the right policy text, and the agent instructions ask for citations, but the citations show only an index reference and never a clickable link to the source document. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The index has no retrievable field that holds the document's source URL, so the tool has no link to place in the citation annotation
The tool's query_type is set to simple, and URL citations are only produced when the tool uses the vector_semantic_hybrid query type
The agent's model doesn't support streaming, and url_citation annotations are only added to responses that are streamed to the client
The tool's top_k value is left at its default, which returns too few documents for the agent to build citations that contain links

stem: A bank wants a production RAG service that calls an Azure AI Search knowledge base and passes the merged grounding content to its own chat model. Compliance allows only generally available features. Which design meets the requirement?

choices.text: Call the retrieve action with the 2026-04-01 REST API and set low retrieval reasoning effort, so an LLM plans subqueries from the chat history
Call the retrieve action with the 2026-04-01 REST API, using intents input and minimal, extractive retrieval against GA knowledge source types
Call the retrieve action with the 2026-04-01 REST API and enable answer synthesis, so the knowledge base returns a cited natural-language answer
Create the knowledge base in the Foundry portal and call it with the messages input, because portal-created objects use the stable GA schema

stem: Engineering PDFs describe approval workflows mostly as embedded diagrams, so a RAG app can't answer process questions from the extracted text. The team wants the diagrams to become searchable text in the same chunk index, using generally available skills. Which pipeline addition fits?

choices.text: Add the Image Analysis skill with the tags feature, so each diagram is indexed with a list of object tags such as "arrow", "box" and "text"
Add the Text Translation skill on normalized images, so the words inside each diagram are translated into the index language and stored
Extract the inline images, run the GenAI Prompt skill to verbalize each image with a chat model, then embed the description with the text
Add the Entity Recognition skill on the extracted images, so the steps and roles shown in each diagram are stored as entity fields in the index

stem: A training company wants its RAG assistant to answer from recorded webinars (MP4) and podcast episodes (MP3) alongside existing PDF chunks in one Azure AI Search index. Which ingestion approach fits?

choices.text: Point a blob indexer at the media container with imageAction set to generateNormalizedImages, so the indexer extracts frames and transcribes the speech
Add the OCR skill to the existing skillset for the media container, so it reads the spoken words and the on-screen text of each recording
Analyze the files with Content Understanding prebuilt-videoSearch and prebuilt-audioSearch, then push transcripts and summaries into the index
Store the recordings as vector fields in the index and let the vectorizer embed the raw audio and video bytes when a query is received

stem: A nightly indexer with integrated vectorization processes thousands of new documents. Some search documents end up without vectors because the Azure OpenAI embedding deployment hit its token-per-minute quota, and the same deployment also serves query-time vectorization. Which two actions follow Learn's guidance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configure a shorter retry interval in the AzureOpenAIEmbedding skill, so the skill retries throttled calls faster until every chunk succeeds
Run the indexer on a schedule (for example every few minutes), so later runs pick up the documents that throttling made the earlier run miss
Switch the vectorizer to a different embedding model with a higher quota, so query traffic no longer counts against the indexing deployment
Remove the Text Split skill, so each document is embedded in one call and the total number of requests to the embedding model goes down
Use separate embedding deployments for indexing and for query vectorization, ideally in different subscriptions, so the two loads don't compete

stem: A consultancy is building RAG ingestion for mixed PDFs, Word files and scanned images. Each file should become clean Markdown with tables, figure descriptions and a short document summary, ready to chunk and embed, with as little custom configuration as possible. Which Content Understanding analyzer should they call?

choices.text: prebuilt-documentFieldSchema, which analyzes each document and proposes a field schema that the team can then use for RAG chunking
prebuilt-document, which is the base analyzer for documents and returns figure descriptions and a summary unless a field schema is added
prebuilt-read, which returns words, paragraphs, formulas and barcodes as Markdown text without needing any model deployment for the analysis
prebuilt-documentSearch, which returns layout-aware Markdown with figure descriptions, annotations and a one-paragraph document summary

stem: A records team needs to convert thousands of scanned reports into text with paragraphs, section structure and tables for a downstream parser. They don't need summaries or fields and have not deployed any chat or embedding model in their Foundry resource. Which Content Understanding analyzer fits?

choices.text: prebuilt-layout, because it returns text with tables, sections and figures through OCR and layout analysis and needs no language model

prebuilt-documentSearch, because it adds figure descriptions and a summary, which also makes its table extraction more accurate than any other analyzer
